purpose: Seed patterns for human-made infographic variation in MDPR visual diversification mode.

flow.description: Used for primary reading order, connecting arrows, and stable pipeline motion.

accent.description: Used for local section identity and normal emphasis.

contrast.description: Used only when an object must read as a point, warning, proof, or editorial interruption.

support.description: Warm or cool surface colors used to avoid one-hue diagrams while preserving coherence.

monotoneIcon.description: A quiet black-or-white icon used only when a text-only slide needs a small visual anchor.

brightnessSequence.rule: Use tint for lower or earlier sequence states, base color for normal emphasis, and shade for current or strongest sequence states.

usageRules: Use monochromatic for ordered depth, progress, ranking, and low-noise technical slides.
Use analogous for neighboring sections that need variation without breaking coherence.
Use complementary for proof points, warnings, validation markers, or other deliberate contrast.
Use split-complementary when a slide needs one strong point plus two supporting accent families.
Use triadic only when three peer categories must be equally visible.
Validate foreground/background pairs with WCAG contrast ratio before final PPTX render.
coherenceRules: Do not express flow only by random hue shifts; use the harmony rule selected by the deck profile.
Same-role arrows and same-depth objects reuse the same harmony purpose unless the flow meaning changes.
Contrast slots are scarce and should appear as point elements, not as section backgrounds.

iconSourcePolicy.licenseRule: Free SVG icons must carry a permissive license record and attribution before being used in a generated deck.
iconSourcePolicy.coherenceRule: Use one icon per text-only support slot, rendered in either black or white, with no multicolor fills.

coherenceRules: uses contrast color only once per local group
label and proof text align to the same left start
seal center aligns to the text group midpoint
minimum text size remains readable in PPT export
inherits parent typography family
uses warm support color instead of a new hue
does not compete with primary flow arrows
same-role nodes share fill and stroke
rail color follows flow role unless a branch has a different meaning
captions align on the reading axis
chip copy stays under four words
contrast color does not repeat as a section color
padding is at least one body line-height horizontally
number role is larger than its label
mini bar uses accent color, not validation contrast
surface depth matches sibling KPI cards
icon is secondary and never replaces the title or body text
use a PowerPoint built-in icon first, otherwise use a licensed free SVG icon
icon tone is black on light backgrounds or white on dark backgrounds
icon center aligns to the adjacent text block midpoint
icon box stays within a side or corner support region and never overlaps text

layoutFamilies.importanceUse: highest importance item becomes the entry node and receives the contrast rim; secondary items share accent rims.
importance controls node diameter, label weight, and whether the node receives a local callout tab.

avoid: different arrow styles for same-role steps

layoutFamilies.importanceUse: highest importance item becomes a lead tile; remaining items become compact rows sorted by importance then source order.

avoid: all rows with equal visual weight
long text without a secondary line break

chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: importance 5 receives the thickest arc, contrast cap, and nearest label; lower-importance values use thinner muted arcs.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Place the primary metric inside or near the ring; keep labels outside the arc tangent with aligned starts.

chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: importance controls needle thickness and whether a callout tab is attached to the dial.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Use a semicircle when labels are short; fall back to ordered-rail when labels exceed the hard limit.

chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: the chart becomes low-contrast background; the most important statement becomes the foreground proof point.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Keep the line graph behind text with opacity below foreground content and no label collision.

inspiredBy: small multiples joined into one story
chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: importance determines which mini-chart becomes enlarged or receives a connector callout.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Use identical mini-chart proportions and a single connector style unless the data flow changes meaning.

chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: highest importance value occupies the center; supporting values orbit as small labels.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Use the ring as a frame, not decoration; every ring layer must map to value, status, or grouping.

chartDiagramFamilies.importanceUse: image object carries the metaphor; the most important value receives a chart overlay or label anchored to the object.
chartDiagramFamilies.layoutRule: Use only when MDPR detects or the user provides a needed image/metaphor; otherwise prefer an abstract chart family.

alignmentLayouts.rule: primary value or concept sits at center; labels align to radial tangent starts with equal safe padding.
long text or explanation stays left; proof, chart, or image anchor stays right with one contrast callout.
same-role objects share width, height, baseline, connector color, and arrow style.
four groups use equal geometry; emphasis is shown by stroke, tab, or lead text, not by resizing one quadrant.

densityRules: If average textChars is above the ideal maximum, prefer ranked-stack over cycle-loop.
If relation is sequence or process and item count is seven or fewer, prefer ordered-rail.
If relation is cycle or feedback and every item fits the cycle hardMax, prefer cycle-loop.
If one item has importance 5 and the rest are 3 or lower, allocate a lead slot instead of equal slots.
If the slide has chart data and needs an image or metaphor, allow pictorial-metaphor-chart; otherwise keep charts abstract and editable.
If trend data has long labels, use line-graph-background with foreground proof text instead of crowded chart labels.
If data is ratio/progress and labels are short, prefer arc-ring-chart or target-ring-frame over a generic bar chart.
If a slide is text-only, medium-or-lower density, and visually too plain, open one monotone-icon-aside support slot instead of adding background decoration.

removeWhen: large decorative container does not encode hierarchy
surface duplicates a visible group panel
